completion_conditions: A PR whose only pushes since the approved head were clean base merges keeps its Guardian approval, disclosed as guardian_comment_carried.

An evil merge, a `merge -s ours`, a forged merge commit, an octopus merge, a superseded second parent, an authored commit, a reversed merge direction, a force-push orphan, a shallow checkout, an edited comment, a multi-SHA body, a retargeted base, a critical risk level and a removed label each independently refuse the carry — and in every one of those cases the Guardian requirement still resolves as required.
With the flag absent, every existing fixture produces a byte-identical result to the pre-change gate.
MergeGate and the deterministic CCA Guardian signal agree on every fixture, and the signal is never more permissive.
The full suite, the guardian-policy, governance-evidence, adversarial and control-plane suites and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: The problem is structural, not incidental. Branch protection has required_status_checks.strict = true, so a BEHIND PR cannot merge. Syncing changes the head SHA. guardian-policy.json sets guardian_comment.require_head_sha = true, and dismiss_stale_reviews is true so a github_review approval is dismissed by the same push. The label survives but the human path needs label AND a head-bound secondary. So every base sync costs a fresh approval.

The carry applies to the guardian_comment source ONLY, as a new source token guardian_comment_carried. Never guardian_label (there is no head binding to carry). Never github_review (GitHub's dismissal IS the Guardian's revocation UI, and a deliberate dismissal is indistinguishable from a stale one in the payload the workflows write). Never external_ai_guardian_review (validate_guardian_policy hard-fails any policy that unbinds it).

The load-bearing proof is tree reproduction, not a diff comparison: `git merge-tree --write-tree <approved head A> <origin/default>` must produce exactly `tree(H)`. This proves every byte at the current head is either Guardian-approved content or content that already reached the default branch through its own gate. Measured: `git merge -s ours <base>` produces an identical DIFF while reverting the base, and an evil merge can carry a payload while touching zero out-of-base paths — so `git diff A H` and patch-equality are both unsafe shortcuts and are explicitly rejected. First-parent membership, no-authored-commits, 2-parent arity and second-parent-ancestry are kept as cheap pre-rejects and as the bound on which A may be named, but they are NOT sufficient alone.

Yield was measured, because a rule that is safe and never fires is worthless. Against the real sync on PR #237 (A=7f34529a…, H=fa826dbe…, base=3bdda917…): first-parent membership PASS, authored commits in A..H = 0, merge arity 2 with the second parent an ancestor of base, and merge-tree reproduced tree(H) exactly (a0566fcc…). Against a synthetic two-consecutive-sync history with disjoint paths: PASS. Against a sync where both sides changed the same file: git conflicts, so the carry is refused and a real operator resolution happens — which is the correct outcome, not a gap.

The residual is accepted and disclosed: proving tree(H) is the mechanical merge does NOT prove the base did not change what the approved code MEANS. It is bounded by refusing the carry for critical risk and for any maintainer-applied high/critical label, and by disclosing the carry as guardian_comment_carried in sources, in the MergeGate warning and in the CCA signal, so nothing downstream reads it as a fresh approval. The alternative bound — requiring the PR's paths and the base's paths to be disjoint — was rejected: measured, 4 of 8 real syncs overlap on .shiki/tasks/*.json, which halves the yield without closing the semantic gap.
Default OFF. Without the explicit flag the code paths are inert and the gate is byte-for-byte today's gate, so a defect degrades to the current behaviour rather than weakening the current one.

No guardian-policy.json key may enable the carry. The policy is loaded from the HEAD checkout, so a head-settable knob would let a PR widen its own approval semantics. The carry is code-pinned, not policy-pinned.

This Goal depends on the four approval-evaluation defects being fixed first. Two of them are load-bearing here: the un-paginated evidence fetch in shiki-mergegate.yml would let a negation comment past page one be invisible to the carry, and the whole-body substring head-SHA test would let a quoted SHA name a carry anchor nobody chose.
grill_with_docs.source: Designed and adversarially attacked 2026-08-01 by a parallel exploration sweep (8 agents: 3 mapping, 4 adversarial lenses, 1 synthesis), then the核心 condition was measured against a real PR sync and a synthetic multi-sync history.

Carrying for critical risk, or when a maintainer label alone resolves high or critical.
Tolerating a merge that required conflict resolution.

outcome: When branch protection forces a stale PR to merge its base in, the Guardian approval already granted for the reviewed content is no longer thrown away. The approval carries if and only if the gate can prove, from git, that every push since the approved head was a mechanical merge of the default branch and changed nothing else. Measured cost today: opening five Contract PRs at once cost four extra operator approvals, one per PR per merge round, purely because main moved.

acceptance_checks: verify_pure_base_sync performs no network or API call, and every git invocation is read-only and runs with cwd=target.
No git invocation in the module has its failure swallowed (no `|| true`, no bare except that continues).
A single clean sync, two consecutive clean syncs, and a base that did not move each prove.
An evil merge is refused by the tree-reproduction step while the first-parent, no-authored-commit and arity steps all PASS — asserted explicitly.
`git merge -s ours <base>` is refused by the tree-reproduction step with the earlier steps passing.
A .gitattributes merge=union is refused before the tree-reproduction step runs.
An octopus merge, an authored non-merge commit, a reversed merge direction, and a second parent that is not an ancestor of the base are each refused by their own step.
A superseded feature tip passes the arity/ancestry step and is refused by tree reproduction.
A commit-tree-forged merge with correct parents and an arbitrary tree is refused.
An orphaned a_sha is refused, with an assertion that no network call was attempted.
A shallow repository is refused with a distinct shallow reason.
An unavailable or failing merge-tree capability probe refuses the carry.
Every test builds a real temporary git repository; git is never mocked.
The module is registered in shiki_installer.py TEMPLATE_PATHS and in test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.

tasks.scope:
Add `scripts/shiki_sync_proof.py` exposing `verify_pure_base_sync(*, target, a_sha, head_sha, default_branch) -> SyncProof`, where `SyncProof` carries `proved: bool`, `reason: str` and the merge count. It is the ONLY module in the guardian family that runs git; every git invocation is read-only, runs with `cwd=target`, and no invocation may be suffixed with `|| true` or have its failure swallowed.

Conditions, in this order, each failure recorded as a distinct reason:
  1. `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is false; `refs/remotes/origin/<default_branch>^{commit}` resolves; `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `head_sha`. A shallow repository is reported distinctly so the caller can fail the step loudly rather than silently not carrying.
  2. Capability probe: `git merge-tree --write-tree <head> <head>` exits 0 and prints 40 hex characters. (Requires git >= 2.38; the probe is what makes an older runner fail closed rather than mysteriously.)
  3. No path named `.gitattributes` exists in the trees of `a_sha`, `head_sha` or the base, and every merge-tree invocation passes `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null`. A `merge=union` attribute can reprogram what a merge produces, which would let a merge be simultaneously 'mechanical' and attacker-chosen.
  4. `a_sha` resolves as a LOCAL object (`git cat-file -e`). Never fall back to any network or API lookup: an API lookup serves commits orphaned by a force-push, which is exactly the case this condition exists to reject.
  5. `a_sha != head_sha` (equal needs no carry).
  6. `a_sha` appears in `git rev-list --first-parent <head_sha>`.
  7. `git rev-list --first-parent --no-merges <a_sha>..<head_sha>` is empty.
  8. Every commit in `git rev-list --first-parent <a_sha>..<head_sha>` has EXACTLY two parents and its second parent is an ancestor of the base.
  9. THE PROOF: `git -c core.attributesFile=/dev/null merge-tree --write-tree <a_sha> <base>` exits 0 (no conflict) and its output equals `git rev-parse <head_sha>^{tree}`.
Any exception is caught at the function boundary and returns `proved=False` with the exception named. There is no branch that returns `proved=True` without step 9 having run and matched.

Register the module in `scripts/shiki_installer.py` TEMPLATE_PATHS and in `scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh`.

Add `tests/test_sync_proof.py` building REAL temporary git repositories — no mocks of git — one per case: a single clean sync proves; two consecutive clean syncs prove; a base that did not move proves; an evil merge (hand-edited merge tree) with a payload in a base-touched path is refused by step 9 while steps 6-8 pass, asserted explicitly so step 9 is proved load-bearing; `git merge -s ours <base>` is refused by step 9 with steps 6-8 passing; a `.gitattributes` with `merge=union` is refused by step 3 BEFORE step 9 runs; an octopus merge is refused by the arity check; an authored non-merge commit after `a_sha` is refused by step 7; a reversed merge (base merged the feature) is refused by step 6; a merge whose second parent is not an ancestor of the base is refused by step 8; a superseded feature tip merged in — reachable from base but stale — passes step 8 and is refused by step 9; a `commit-tree`-forged merge with an arbitrary tree and correct parents is refused by step 9; an orphaned `a_sha` is refused by step 4 with an assertion that no network call was attempted; a shallow clone is refused with the distinct shallow reason.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task builds, and what to change to get the same result.
  Problem: branch protection has `required_status_checks.strict = true`, so a PR that goes BEHIND must merge its base in before it can merge; that changes the head SHA; and `guardian_comment.require_head_sha` is true, so the approval already granted for the reviewed content is discarded. Measured on 2026-08-01: landing five Contract PRs cost four extra operator approvals, one per PR per merge round, with no content change whatsoever between them.
  Why tree reproduction and not a diff: measured in throwaway repositories — `git merge -s ours <base>` yields an identical `git diff A H` while reverting the base entirely, and an evil merge can carry a payload while touching zero paths outside those the base itself touched. Both defeat every cheaper check. Step 9 is the criterion; steps 6-8 are pre-rejects and bound which `a_sha` may be named.
  Measured yield, so the rule is known to fire: on the real PR #237 sync (A=7f34529a72a14c076adae67bee1cd8a390ce8df0, H=fa826dbe0b5a5670cf0aa5994f042e7592ff41d2, base=3bdda917d6e1f3e879a55f6eb7c7478640e8d896) with git 2.54.0, step 6 PASS, step 7 count 0, step 8 arity 2 with the second parent an ancestor of base, and step 9 produced a0566fcca76b075a48693e461921efe616ea1408 which equals tree(H) exactly. A synthetic two-sync history with disjoint paths also proved. A sync where both sides edited the same file conflicts, so the carry is refused and the operator resolves it — the correct outcome.
  Known landmine: `git merge-tree --write-tree` needs git >= 2.38 and the runner's version is NOT verified by this repository. That is why the capability probe is a condition rather than an assumption: an older runner must refuse the carry loudly, never silently mis-prove one.
  Reproducible when: every attack case above is refused with the step that refused it named, and the real #237 shape proves.

tasks.scope:
Introduce the source token `guardian_comment_carried`. It is produced only when a candidate approved head is proved by `verify_pure_base_sync`, and it joins the human-secondary set alongside `github_review` and `guardian_comment` — so the label leg is still required and removing the label remains a working revocation lever.

Gating conditions evaluated BEFORE the git proof, each refusing the carry with a distinct reason:
  - The feature is OFF unless `--base-sync-carry` is passed AND `--default-branch` is non-empty. Absent either, every code path is inert.
  - Resolved Guardian risk is exactly `high`. `critical` never carries. If the PR's LABELS alone resolve high or critical, the carry is refused — a maintainer escalating by label must get a fresh approval.
  - The PR's `baseRefName` equals the default branch, and no `base_ref_changed` entry appears anywhere in the timeline feed.
  - Candidate extraction runs in the EXISTING `_comment_source` order — marker, not-negating, actor configured, author allowed — and only then extracts the SHA. A comment from a non-configured actor is never parsed.
  - The carrying comment is unedited (`updated_at == created_at`, or `updated_at` absent).
  - Only the newest candidate by (created_at, feed index) is eligible. Any comment from a configured Guardian carrying a negation marker with `created_at` at or after the candidate's refuses the carry AND raises a HARD blocker — routed through `_comment_source`'s blockers channel so it survives the demotion the caller applies to soft blockers.

Wire `--base-sync-carry` and `--default-branch` into `scripts/mergegate_check.py` (argparse, `enforce_guardian_policy`, and BOTH call sites — the contract-mode one and the normal-path one; missing either makes the feature unreachable on that path), `scripts/guardian_approval_signal.py` (argparse, the evaluate call, and the emitted JSON, which gains `carried_from_head` and `carry_refused_reasons`), `scripts/shiki_guardian_status.py` (so the operator-facing and CCA-posted status cannot contradict the gate) and the `guardian status` subparser in `scripts/shiki_cli.py`.

The proof is recomputed in-process in every judging invocation. It is never written to `.shiki/gha` and never carried in an artifact, so there is nothing to go stale or be forged.

Add `tests/test_guardian_carry.py` driving the real evaluator, and `tests/test_guardian_carry_parity.py` asserting MergeGate and the signal return identical approved/sources over one fixture set and that the signal is never more permissive. Positive cases assert both `approved` and that `guardian_comment_carried` is in `sources`. EVERY negative case must assert BOTH that the carry did not happen AND that the Guardian requirement still resolves as required — the signal reporting `required=true, approved=false`, and MergeGate blocking with a Guardian blocker string — never merely a non-zero exit. Cover: a fresh current-head comment still wins over a carry; critical risk refuses; a label-only high escalation refuses; a retargeted base refuses; a `base_ref_changed` timeline entry refuses; an edited comment refuses; a body with two SHAs refuses; a non-configured actor is dropped before extraction; a later negation comment refuses AND produces a hard blocker, asserted not to be a warning; a removed label defeats approval; an empty `--default-branch` behaves exactly as the pre-change gate; the flag omitted entirely produces a byte-identical result on the full existing fixture set; a comment from another PR is never a candidate; and no invented guardian-policy.json key can enable the carry.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task changes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a PR whose content nobody touched loses its approval because branch protection made it merge main. Measured 2026-08-01 across five Contract PRs: four extra operator approvals, entirely mechanical.
  Why the carry must reach BOTH the gate and the signal: the MergeGate policy job depends on the CCA job, `enforce_cca_verdict` fails any verdict that is not complete, and the signal the CCA prompt reads is computed from the guardian evaluation alone. Wiring the carry into MergeGate only means the CCA still returns needs_guardian, its job fails, and the policy check never runs — the gate this change exists to move is never reached. This exact duality has been undercounted repeatedly in this repository; both call sites inside mergegate_check.py have the same property.
  Why the label leg is still required: the label is the operator's revocation lever that does not depend on any SHA. Keeping it means an operator can always kill a carried approval by removing one label.
  Why a negation must be a HARD blocker: the caller demotes soft blockers to warnings once any approval path succeeds, so a revocation routed as a soft blocker would be silently swallowed by the very carry it is trying to revoke.
  Reproducible when: a base-synced PR keeps its approval with `guardian_comment_carried` in sources, and every listed attack refuses the carry while leaving the Guardian requirement required.

BACKWARD-COMPATIBILITY CONSTRAINT (audited 2026-08-04): every new parameter added to `evaluate_guardian_approval` and to the functions the signal/status paths call MUST be keyword-only WITH a default. Out-of-lock callers exist and must keep working unchanged: `scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh`, `tests/test_guardian_evidence.py`, `tests/test_guardian_status.py`, `tests/test_guardian_signal*.py`, `tests/test_contract_approval.py`, `tests/test_bookkeeping_closeout.py`. A positional or required parameter breaks all of them and the task cannot repair them from inside its locks.
